Nick Boyle: Boyle enters the season with the look of a quarterback ready for the next step. Michigan’s projected top pick brings two years of steady production, experience in a pro-style offense and the intelligence to adjust at the line before the snap.
Dannie Montano: When the pocket changes shape, Montano can turn a breakdown into an opportunity. The North Dakota State quarterback returns with a productive résumé, a strong arm and impressive numbers on throws outside the pocket, giving scouts plenty to watch this season.
Micah Howard: Receivers looking for separation may find Howard waiting at every turn. Stanford’s corner combines sharp football intelligence with the ability to mirror routes step for step, giving him the early profile of a shutdown defender and a leading non-quarterback prospect.
Dylan Smith: Georgia’s latest defensive line standout has the size to command attention. At 6-foot-5, Smith brings an eye-catching physical profile and a productive season to build on, with the potential to become the most impressive player in a line of highly regarded prospects.
Trey Sternberg: Sternberg brings two very different kinds of trouble to an interior defender. Iowa’s guard plays with the edge to set a physical tone in the run game, then settles into elite pass protection. That combination gives an offense a formidable presence inside.
Jaylen Scruggs: A defender can have Scruggs surrounded and still struggle to get a hand on him. Alabama’s dynamic receiver combines elite speed with sudden changes of direction, giving an offense a playmaker who can create space in the tightest situations and threaten from anywhere.
Ramello Williams: Williams comes off the edge with more than one way to reach the quarterback. The Texas rusher brings a broad menu of moves and two seasons of sack and pressure production, giving offensive tackles plenty to prepare for as another year approaches.
Tremon Henderson II: Henderson has the size and coverage tools to make an entire side of the field feel smaller. Clemson’s corner brings the physical skill set to take on demanding assignments, giving scouts a defender to watch closely as the new season unfolds.
Tyler Smit: Smit gives Indiana a downfield target who can win before the ball is snapped and after it arrives. The big receiver pairs an elite release with contested-catch ability and a nose for the end zone, making him a dangerous vertical option.
Amani Okonkwo: Okonkwo brings a track star’s speed and a sturdy frame to the Ole Miss passing game. He can get behind corners in a hurry, then use his strength to bounce off contact, giving an offense a compact deep threat with explosive potential.
